i.norm: Tests that using {@link IntUnaryOperator#identity()} as the RNG causes an {@link IndexOutOfBoundsException} when generating a string from a restricted character pool. When {@code selectFrom} is called with two null characters ('\0', '\0'), the builder deduplicates them into a character set of size 1. The identity operator returns its input unchanged, so {@code identity.applyAsInt(1) == 1}, which is used as the list index. Since the list has only one element (index 0), accessing index 1 throws {@link IndexOutOfBoundsException}.
Build a generator restricted to two null chars ('\0', '\0'). After deduplication the effective character pool has size 1.
identity(n) == n, so it returns the pool size instead of a valid index
Requesting a large string triggers the broken index immediately: identity.applyAsInt(1) == 1, but characterList.get(1) is out of bounds.
